Statistical inference typically consists of two steps:

1. fitting a statistical model to data;
2. summarizing our uncertainty about the parameters of the fitted model,
   based on the data (and, in Bayesian inference, on prior beliefs).

There are two predominant paradigms for statistical inference:

- [frequentist inference](intro-MLEs.qmd#sec-intro-MLEs),
  which treats parameters as fixed unknown constants;
- [Bayesian inference](bayesian-inference.qmd),
  which treats parameters as random variables with prior distributions.
